title: The Cracks in the Rock and the Marketplace
english: Worthy of the food... 'the truths were becoming real' (12:3d). And those 'looking in the eye-sockets' will darken. These 'looking in the eye-sockets' are the souls using the senses. For the senses are to be taken as 'eye-sockets'. Therefore, those 'looking in the eye-sockets' will 'darken'. For when the sensible things pass away, then darkness will prevail; they no longer see those sensible things as they ought; is there anything left besides the loss of accurate perception?

It is also possible to take it this way: those 'searching the Scriptures' and 'paying attention to the reading' of them find 'eye-sockets', through which they are able to be enlightened, and the light that exists within. Therefore, these 'looking in the eye-sockets' 'were darkened' because they are no longer 'becoming real'. But the 'becoming real' ones split the seeds, making 'eye-sockets'. Take the investigation of the Scriptures and their clarity by analogy with the splitting of the seeds which makes the 'eye-socket'; and this is also what it means for them to 'become real'.

And it can be said differently: they say that those 'looking in the eye-sockets' seem to see much; and some are able to approach the light; and despite the inability and the weakness of the sight, a perception of the light occurs. When, therefore, the hidden light is produced again, those 'looking' are 'darkened' through certain 'eye-sockets'. They are not able to see the light, having those small 'eye-sockets'. But when their body changes from the 'perishable' to the 'imperishable' and from the 'psychic' to the 'spiritual', they no longer have 'darkening' senses, but renewed and increasing ones.

Therefore, the 'darkening of those looking in the eye-sockets' does not bring complete injury; for when they 'are darkened', they will see things more clearly according to the argument of 'the part', so that their own 'eye-socket' of 'the part' is not 'abolished' by becoming a great opening. And it is possible to take it this way because 'the eye-sockets' is in the plural. A praiseworthy 'eye-socket' is brought forward in the singular in the Mosaic writings, when he received a desire to 'see the face' of God and to see Him clearly and 'knowingly'. God said to him that, being still a 'man', he 'is not able' to possess the brightness (Exodus 33:20); 'but I place you in the opening of the rock' (Exodus 33:22), regarding one 'rock' as an 'eye-socket'. And 'the rock is Christ' from that...

Regarding the 'rock' and the openings in Christ. For they are called 'rocks' in the plural and 'crevices'. 'The spirit crushes the rocks'. And it is said concerning the devil: 'The pride of your heart has carried you away to dwell in the crevices of the rocks' (Job 13:16)—not 'in the crevice of the rock', for that is blessed—but because they pay attention to antichrists and false teachers and false prophets, the 'crevice' of those is not for seeing but rather for harming. 'Fissures of rocks' indeed are called 'crevices' in other places; and the discord of the teaching is a 'schism' and a multitude of 'crevices'. Therefore, those 'looking' in the 'crevice' do not 'gaze darkly', but rather are enlightened. But those in the many 'crevices' who seem to see are 'darkened'. When the truth comes into the midst, every deception is loosed; and in the deception were the many 'crevices'. And as they often said the image of the division, that those failing the vote of 349 say ten thousand 'rocks'. If therefore the correct vote shines upon, that which those voting wrongly said is loosed. Thus those holding false doctrines, in the absence of the truth, become so; when this shines and illuminates, all those holding false doctrines are loosed.

12,4ab And they will shut doors in the marketplace in the weakness of the voice of the truth. 12,4a I spoke concerning human matters, those 'being seen and being timely'. Concerning the coming age and the end of the present age he teaches and says that 'they will shut doors in the marketplace' (Acts 19:41). And 'marketplace' here he means the church, as the rhetoricians say. As long as this life exists, the 'marketplaces' or the 'marketplace', the church, exist, in which those who speak are speaking. But 'it will be shut' after these things, when teaching is no longer present in the 'time of judgment'. I do not say this to mean that there will not be instruction in the ages to come, but according to that 'time' in which those being judged 'stand at the judgment seat of Christ' (2 Timothy 4:1); for they have a word regarding what has been done, regarding being instructed or being taught. And if ever the labor from the... [gap]... another word is not instruction being brought forth by men or angels... concerning the ten virgins in the parable it is said that the...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Closing of the Marketplace
english: The five who have gathered oil, pressed from the true olive tree, possessing that which provides nourishment and illuminates, entered with the bridegroom into the banquet when a cry occurred in the middle of the night: 'The bridegroom comes, go out to meet him' (Matt 25:6). But those who did not take oil in the vessels, having neglected the one who guards the light, went out to buy and no longer found those selling them; for it was no longer a place of instruction then, nor were those selling the divine words present. And because of this, they remained outside.

And here, therefore, when the village is gathered, the 'marketplaces' are 'closed'; they do not have those 'open doors' about which the divine words write. For indeed the apostle says: 'A great and effective door has been opened to me, and there are many who oppose me' (1 Cor 16:9). If the 'great door' of the word is 'opened' and 'effective', then 'many who oppose' are present. And it is 'effective' when those who hear convert the teachings into works. And 'many' become 'opposing'; for if we observe the Scriptures, it is not always that false prophets are found when they are prophets, nor are false apostles present at other times when they are apostles and teachers. For, envying, they 'oppose' and attempt to contradict the truth, attempting to contradict those who teach well, sometimes even attacking them and leading them to death. Therefore, a 'door' 'has been opened to me, great and effective'. It is not that the 'marketplace' was 'shut', but the 'doors' of the 'marketplace' were not 'open'.

And in another epistle of his he says: 'After I had come and a door had been opened, I had no respite for my spirit, not finding Titus my brother' (Col 4:3). Before the 'door was opened', he 'had no respite' so as to bring forward the word without finding those who cooperate with him. And in the proverbs it is said: 'Blessed is the man who listens to me, and the man who, if he keeps my ways, remains watchful at my doors by day' (Prov 8:34). The 'doors' of wisdom are the 'doors' of the 'marketplace'. Therefore the 'doors' in the 'marketplace' are 'closed' when the place of instruction is gathered. And see that they 'close' the 'doors' voluntarily. The 'closing' of the 'doors' is not by force.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Proclamation of the Resurrection
english: It must be said, because of the truth, what is the inherent nature of things. What then are those 'closing the marketplace'? They are the teachers. This is similar to what is said in Isaiah, though rather according to a different thought than the literal words: 'I am being finished by the clouds so that no rain falls upon it'; for from receiving the 'rain', they were turning the 'thorns' and the 'thistles' into plants, but the intention of the 'clouds' and what was commanded to them was that the 'vineyard might bring forth brief grapes'; but since instead of 'grapes' they had grown 'thorns', not wishing to increase the evil again by stinginess, He 'commanded' them 'not to rain'.

In this way also these [teachers], since they no longer had those whom they ought to teach, 'closed the doors in the marketplaces'. And this happens in this way many times, for when the teachers hear: 'Do not give the holy thing to the dogs, nor cast pearls before the swine, lest turning they throw them upon you and trample you' (Matt 7:6). Toward this, again, 'it is not given to those'. For they were about to be more impious, 'trampling' the divine words which are the 'pearls', [and] decorating the 'inner man' with [worldly] things; not even observing the beauty or the preciousness of them, they were about to 'trample' them instead of regarding them highly. So in a certain way they 'close the doors in the marketplace' here; and if so here, much more there, until the judgment seat and the tribunal be 'opened'.

'And the daughters of song shall rise up to the voice of a sparrow, and all the daughters of song shall be humbled' (Ps 47:6). The 'marketplace' will 'rise up to the voice of a sparrow'. Those 'knowing in part and prophesying' 'closed' the 'marketplace' and its 'doors'. These are the 'apostles', the 'prophets', the 'teachers' among men. Let us show that even the spiritual [beings] 'sent for ministry' are 'withdrawn' 'to the voice of a sparrow'. A 'sparrow' may be said to be the Savior here according to the man, according to: 'And I became as a sparrow upon a roof' (Matt 24:32). And each of the birds, when 'having heard the words' of Jesus, turns them into works and 'builds a house' and fills the building and crowns the building, cries out 'upon the roof' in vigilance.

As if raising the 'voice'. The proclamation of the truth can also be called a 'sparrow' then, becoming lofty, since it once happened below for the hearers. But since now even the perfect hearers have become inspired and pursue the things above, there the 'sparrow upon the roof' cries out to them; the perfect has cried out, happening above the world, to face 'face to face' with the truth.

'Rising to the voice of the sparrow', since it is also possible for them themselves to 'rise' concerning which the word speaks according to the expected resurrection. The proclamation of the resurrection signifies one thing in many ways. For when it is compared to a 'trumpet'—'the trumpet shall sound and the dead shall rise incorruptible' (1 Cor 15:52)—this trumpeter is the herald of the resurrection, calling so that all having heard the summons may 'rise'. For this reason it is compared to a 'trumpet'. And this instrument is loud-voiced and is heard everywhere. Thus also here the proclamation of the resurrection said 'sparrow', which seems not to be undignified.

The 'rising ones' are 'being raised', but instead of 'corruptible' they are 'incorruptible', instead of 'dishonorable' and 'weak' they are 'strong' and 'glorious', instead of 'psychic' they are 'spiritual'. Therefore, there will be a 'rising into the voice of the sparrow'. But how will that 'marketplace' which was 'closed' 'rise'? It will 'rise' in the whole world.

I say this: that proclamation being made public here changes from being 'in part' 'prophecy or knowledge' (1 Cor 13:9) but becomes 'face to face'. This is the 'rising' according to the former dispensation. But what kind of 'time' shall we receive? The time of 'judgment'. But in what 'time' is it 'closed'? When the present age reaches its end. In this... the beginning and the end are one. The end of this day brings the beginning of the next... there is no separating time from time. Therefore, what is called 'now', which they say is noteworthy and the boundary of time, is the end of the past, the future of the present, and again the end of the present and the beginning of the future. If I say this, I say judgment and resurrection together; and it seems that the beginning is the end of the resurrection.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
